slides.headline: Couples who stayed affectionate for longer after sex *reported higher satisfaction.*
slides.body: Cuddling, talking, closeness. Both their sexual and relationship satisfaction were higher, and still were three months later.
slides.note: Source: Muise, Giang & Impett, _Archives of Sexual Behavior_, 2014. 335 people in relationships and 101 couples, Canada. A link, not proof.

slides.headline: The messages can wait. *Your person is right here.*
slides.body: Turn the phone face down, or leave it in another room. Ten quiet minutes is plenty.

slides.headline: About nothing. About everything. *About what you loved.*
slides.body: No rush to shower, sleep or scroll. This is the part where people feel chosen.

slides.headline: Don’t rush off. *The closeness after counts.*
slides.lead: Send this to your person. Tonight, stay a while.

captions.instagram:
The minutes after matter too. 🤍

In a Canadian study of 335 people in relationships and 101 couples, those who spent longer being affectionate after sex (cuddling, talking, closeness) reported higher sexual and relationship satisfaction, and still did three months later. A link, not proof.

So tonight: phone face down, stay close, and talk. About nothing, about everything, about what you loved.

Send this to your person.

Source: Muise, Giang & Impett, Archives of Sexual Behavior, 2014.

#IntimovaTips #Couples #Relationships #Intimacy #NoShame #Intimova
